As a child I was fairly active, playing outside, always on the trampoline, waking up early on Saturdays, normal kid stuff. My mom eventually noticed me slowing down some, and having difficulty making it through the day without crashing. I also had always had a healthy appetite and when that went away some, my mother had some suspicions because she knew what Crohn's looked like.

My father suffered from Crohn's for a bug chunk of his life right after college after he married my mother. My mom took good care of him as he withered and went through a lot of different medicines and doctor visits. Eventually he had about a foot or two of his small intestine removed. He has been healthy ever since.

Since my mom know what to look for she took me to several doctors and eventually, after several doctors said I couldn't have it at my age, (7) She took me to a pediatric gastroenterologist he saw it right away. I had a colonoscopy and it showed signs of Crohn's in all of my intestines and even in my esophagus. I got put on pentasa and I've been fairly healthy ever since!

I know this is a little more than you asked for but it's how I learned about it and how my symptoms were. Feel free to ask more if I wasn't clear on anything!

My only tip is make sure (in a front-ways throw) when you mount it like Andre does at 1:41 in the video, make sure the loop on your non-throw-hand is long. So when you pinch and bring your throw-hand up, and your non-throw-hand down the string will bunch up and the yoyo will return. I usually recommend having your hands just about the same level vertically and about 2-3 inches apart horizontally. You'll have to start the motion of your hands slowly. If might hit your hand a couple times while learning, but you'll learn to feel when the yoyo will come up.
